title: Best Ulam Constants for Higher-Order Linear Difference Equations in the Hyperbolic Case
content: For constant-coefficient linear difference equations on the nonnegative integers with values in a nonzero real or complex Banach space, this paper determines the best Ulam constant whenever no characteristic root lies on the unit circle. Yuan, Xu and Brzdęk (2025) established a Green-function Ulam bound in this hyperbolic setting. When at least two distinct characteristic roots occur and at least one lies inside the unit circle, it remained unknown whether the bound was optimal or a best constant existed. The Green bound is shown to be optimal for every hyperbolic root configuration, with the best constant equal to the \( \ell^1\ \)-norm of the associated Green kernel. The proof combines uniform exponential decay of bounded homogeneous solutions with finitely supported perturbations, shifted far along the half-line and phase-aligned to approach the bound. The argument establishes optimality without assuming uniqueness of a nearby exact solution. The qualitative criterion for strong Hyers–Ulam stability was already known. The result here supplies the exact constant in every stable case.
